templates.title: Article
templates.use: A general non-fiction piece for a publication or blog.
structure: Introduction: what this is for the reader

templates.title: Essay
templates.use: An argument or analysis that makes and supports a point.
structure: Body paragraph 1: topic sentence + evidence + explanation
Conclusion: restate the point and why it matters

templates.title: Blog post
templates.use: A scannable online piece for readers who skim.

templates.title: Report
templates.use: A factual document that summarises findings for a reader or client.

templates.title: Business email
templates.use: A clear, professional email that gets a response.
structure: A clear next step or deadline

templates.title: Cover letter
templates.use: A short letter introducing you for a role or opportunity.
structure: What you can do for them

templates.title: Personal statement
templates.use: A short piece that explains who you are and why it matters for your application.
structure: Who I am and my goal
A specific experience that shaped me
What I learned and how I grew

templates.title: Review
templates.use: An honest assessment of a product, book, film or place.
structure: What it is and who it is for

templates.title: Case study
templates.use: A detailed account of a real example that teaches a lesson.

templates.title: Research paper
templates.use: Formal academic work that reports original analysis.

templates.title: Short story
templates.use: A compact fiction built for a single effect.

templates.title: Journal entry
templates.use: Private reflective writing.

templates.title: Memo
templates.use: A brief internal note to a team or manager.

templates.title: Proposal
templates.use: A document that proposes a plan or a piece of work.
structure: Why you are the right choice

templates.title: Press release
templates.use: An announcement sent to the media.
structure: Lead paragraph: who, what, when, where, why

templates.title: Newsletter
templates.use: A regular email update to readers or subscribers.

templates.title: Product description
templates.use: Copy that sells one product clearly.

templates.title: Tutorial
templates.use: A step-by-step guide that teaches someone to do a task.

templates.title: Annotated bibliography
templates.use: A source list where each entry is followed by a short summary and assessment.
structure: Full citation in your required style (APA, MLA or Chicago)
Summary: what the source argues or reports, in 2–3 sentences
Assessment: how credible and how relevant it is
Reflection: how you will actually use it in your work
Repeat per source, ordered alphabetically by author

templates.title: Meeting agenda
templates.use: Circulated before a meeting so people arrive knowing what will be decided.
structure: Meeting title, date, time and location or link
Purpose: the one thing this meeting must achieve
Item 1 — topic, who leads, time allotted, decision needed
Item 2 — topic, who leads, time allotted, decision needed

templates.title: Meeting minutes
templates.use: A record of what was decided and who owes what afterwards.
structure: Item: discussion summarised in a few neutral lines
Decision: what was agreed, stated plainly
Action: who does it, and by when

templates.title: Reference letter
templates.use: A recommendation you write for someone else — for a job, a course or a tenancy.
structure: Your name, role and contact details
How you know the person, and for how long
What they did, with one concrete example
Any honest reservation, if the letter must be balanced
Offer to be contacted, and sign off

templates.title: Formal complaint letter
templates.use: A calm, factual complaint to a company or institution that is more likely to be acted on.
structure: Your details, their details, the date
Reference: account, order or case number
What happened, in dated order and without adjectives
What you want them to do — be specific and reasonable
What you will do next if there is no reply

templates.title: Podcast script and show notes
templates.use: An episode plan you can actually read aloud, plus the notes that get published with it.
structure: Intro: show name, host, what this episode covers
Segment 3 — the turn or the counterpoint
Show notes: links, guests and credits

templates.title: Occasion speech (wedding, tribute, eulogy)
templates.use: A short spoken piece for a moment that matters, where tone is harder than structure.
structure: Who you are and your connection to the person
The opening line — concrete, not a general statement
One specific story that shows rather than tells
What that story reveals about them
A second, shorter beat — often gentle humour, or the turn to seriousness
What they mean to the people in the room
A closing line the room can hold on to

templates.title: Crowdfunding pitch
templates.use: A campaign page that explains the thing, the need and the ask without overpromising.
structure: One-sentence description of what you are making or funding
The problem, stated in human terms
Your solution, and why it works
Who you are and why you can deliver it
Exactly what the money pays for, itemised
Risks and what happens if things slip
The ask, and how to share it
